report.releaseDate: 6–9 Nov 2026 (NYSGC statewide monthly reports for October 2026)
report.verdict: October 2026 was a record volume month for New York's mobile sportsbooks ($2.79bn handle, GGR $258.1m, 51% tax = $131.7m) and the first October in which Resorts World NYC reported as a full commercial casino, lifting statewide casino GGR 248% to $194.9m — but the underlying story is a high-tax, slow-to-liberalise market: FYTD mobile GGR is down ~3% on weaker hold, VLT net win is being cannibalised by RWNYC's conversion, iGaming is dead until at least 2027, and the state is simultaneously fighting prediction markets in court and its own flagship casino over $80.6m of unpaid racing-support levies. For an operator, New York is scale without margin: the largest US sports-betting pool, an eight-operator oligopoly where FanDuel/DraftKings hold 71% of handle, and a 51% GGR tax that leaves little room for a new entrant.
summary: **Regulator and framework.** The New York State Gaming Commission (NYSGC; chair Brian O'Dwyer, executive director Robert Williams) regulates commercial casinos (Racing, Pari-Mutuel Wagering and Breeding Law, Art. 13, authorised by the 2013 constitutional amendment permitting up to seven commercial casinos), mobile sports wagering (2021 budget law; live since 8 Jan 2022), video lottery gaming (Tax Law §1612), the NY Lottery, pari-mutuel racing/ADW and charitable gaming. Tribal Class III gaming (Seneca, Oneida, St Regis Mohawk) sits under federal compacts and publishes no GGR — treat as n/a.

**Market size, October 2026.** Reported regulated win across the three NYSGC-published verticals was ~$585m (est., sum of parts): mobile sports GGR $258.1m, commercial casino GGR $194.9m (incl. $0.6m retail sports) and VLT net win $132.1m. The comparable October 2025 figure was ~$505m (est.), i.e. +16% YoY, but ~two-thirds of the increase is the reclassification of Resorts World NYC (RWNYC) from VLT to commercial casino plus its new live table games, not organic growth.

**Mobile sports wagering set a US record.** Handle of $2,787,474,078 (+5.5% YoY vs $2.64bn in Oct-25, the prior record; +16.1% MoM vs $2.40bn) with GGR of $258,123,128 (+8.1% YoY), the third-highest month since launch. Hold was 9.26% vs 9.04% a year ago and only 6.6% in September. Net revenue to education (the 51% tax plus $33.6k of prior-period adjustments) was $131,676,346, up from $121.8m in Oct-25.

**But fiscal-year revenue is going backwards on hold.** April–October 2026 handle of $15.35bn is +6.7% YoY ($14.39bn), yet GGR of $1.37bn is ~3.5% below the $1.41bn of the same months in 2025 because hold slipped to 8.90% from 9.83%. Fiscal tax receipts are $25.1m behind the FY2025/26 pace at the half-year, even though calendar-year tax has already topped $1bn for the third straight year.

**Operator landscape — a two-firm market with Fanatics as the only mover.** Eight licensees: FanDuel $1,022.7m handle (36.7% share; GGR $113.9m, 44.1% of GGR, 11.14% hold), DraftKings $948.7m (34.0%; GGR $81.9m, -1.2%; 8.63% hold), Fanatics $321.4m (+56.3% YoY, 11.5% share; GGR $24.0m), BetMGM $218.2m (+16.4%; $15.6m), Caesars $175.6m (flat; $13.1m), BetRivers $50.5m (-4.8%; $4.5m), theScore Bet $35.9m (-40.5% vs ESPN Bet's Oct-25; $3.6m) and Bally Bet $14.5m (-12.3%; $1.5m). FanDuel+DraftKings = 70.7% of handle (73.6% a year ago); Fanatics took ~80% of the market's $144.8m YoY handle increase.

**Commercial casino GGR trebled on RWNYC's conversion.** Five commercial casinos won $194.9m (+248% vs $56.0m; +5.8% vs $184.3m in September): slots/ETG $135.3m (+214.1%), table games $58.3m (+399.6%), poker $0.74m, retail sports $0.59m. RWNYC alone took $134.3m (69% of the total; slots/ETG $89.3m, tables $45.0m on an average 275 tables vs 242 in September). The four upstate casinos won $60.6m (+8.2% YoY): Rivers Schenectady $20.2m (+14.2%), Resorts World Catskills $15.7m (+10.6%), del Lago $15.0m (+3.9%), Tioga Downs $9.7m (+0.5%).

**Casino tax take $78.8m — and our bottom-up reconciliation matches exactly.** Applying RWNYC's bid rates (56% slots / 30% tables) and the upstate rates (30% slots/ETG, 10% tables, poker and sports) to October's product split yields $63.5m + $15.3m = $78.8m, the NYSGC-reported figure. Effective statewide rate 40.4% of GGR; RWNYC's effective rate ~47%.

**RWNYC is tracking well below its bid.** Since reporting as a commercial casino in April, RWNYC has generated $794.3m GGR through October (monthly range $122–136m since May); its application projected $2.2bn of GGR by 2027 versus a current ~$1.5–1.6bn run-rate (est.). Between May and October it lifted average daily slots/ETGs 61% to 4,024 but machine revenue fell 9.5% and win per unit per day dropped from $1,275 to $716 — classic floor-expansion dilution. Through 15 Nov the property had 4,137 machines and 345 tables.

**Downstate licensing is done, but two of three resorts are years away.** The NYSGC unanimously awarded all three downstate licences on 15 Dec 2025: RWNYC (Genting; $5.5bn expansion), Metropolitan Park (Hard Rock/Steve Cohen, Willets Point; $8.1bn) and Bally's Bronx (Ferry Point; $4bn) — $17.6bn of committed investment and a $500m minimum licence fee each. Metropolitan Park and Bally's target 2030 openings; the board's consultants projected $5.5bn of combined annual GGR by 2033 and ~$7bn of incremental gaming tax over 2027–36. NYC's Public Design Commission has twice deferred its design vote on Metropolitan Park (late Oct, 23 Nov); a third attempt is set for 30 Nov, and a residents' lawsuit against the licence (filed 20 Mar 2026) is pending.

**Tax regime by vertical.** Mobile sports: 51% of GGR (cash basis), $25m one-off licence fee per operator, 10-year term [licence fee/term from the enabling statute, not re-verified this session]. Retail sports at casinos: 10% of GGR. Upstate casinos: 30% slots/ETG (all four petitioned down from 37–45% under the 2021 amendment), 10% tables; 80% of tax to education/property-tax relief, 10% host municipality/county, 10% regional counties. Downstate: statutory minimum 25% slots / 10% tables — RWNYC bid 56%/30%, Metropolitan Park 25%/10%, Bally's 30%/10%, with downstate proceeds split between education and the MTA. VLTs: tiered statutory split of net win (Empire City: education 54–60%, agent commission 26–32%, 10% marketing allowance, 4% racing support).

**The racing-support dispute is the live fiscal risk.** Downstate licensees must fund >$150m a year of horse-racing support payments to NYRA; because its rivals will not open until ~2030, RWNYC bears the whole obligation (>$500m cumulatively). Genting argues the levy sits inside its 56% slot rate and has been netting it against tax, leaving $80.6m of arrears through October, rising ~$13m a month and potentially >$180m by June 2027; paying both would push its effective slot burden to ~72%. An October interim agreement has RWNYC paying NYRA directly, but the state has not conceded the deficiency, the MTA stands to lose up to ~$150m, and RWNYC has threatened to shelve its $3.3bn expansion. The deal lapses at the end of the June 2027 legislative session.

**VLT net win fell 37% to $132.1m on the RWNYC reclassification; +4% like-for-like** across 11,373 machines at the eight remaining facilities (+5.8% MoM). Empire City (MGM, Yonkers) led with $52.26m (+2.5% YoY, +7.6% MoM; 4,516 VGMs at $373 win/unit/day; $26.4m to education, $20.6m agent commission), Jake's 58 (Suffolk OTB) $26.0m; Saratoga ran ~$13.6m in September. Empire City did not bid for a downstate licence and remains a VLT facility.

**Lottery.** NY Lottery sales were $565.5m for the four weeks to 31 October, including $307.5m of instant tickets; the Lottery remains the largest US state lottery and all VLT education contributions flow through it. Full-FY sales: n/a in this review.

**iGaming is off the table until 2027 at the earliest.** Sen. Addabbo's S2614 (online slots/table games, NYSGC licensing, in-state live-dealer studios, ~$475m/yr projected tax) was shelved before the 4 June 2026 session close after Gov. Hochul declined to engage; her office said only that she would 'review any legislation that passes'. No regulated online casino exists; NYSGC licensing covers land-based casinos, VLTs, racing, lottery and mobile sports only.

**Prediction markets are the state's enforcement front.** NYSGC issued a cease-and-desist to Kalshi on 24 Oct 2025; a federal judge denied Kalshi's emergency injunction; the Attorney General and Governor sued Kalshi in state court on 31 Jul 2026 (injunction, disgorgement, treble fines — press tallies ≥$36bn incl. $100k per illegal bet), the AG sued Coinbase and Gemini on 21 Apr 2026 and has moved against Polymarket. On 23 Nov 2026 Justice Melissa Crane denied the AG's TRO, leaving sports contracts live in New York pending a January 2027 hearing. S9414 (ban on sports/election contracts) cleared committee 6–0 on 20 May 2026 but never reached the floor.

**Other direction of travel.** New York has enacted a ban on online sweepstakes casinos (new RPWBL §912) [enacted late 2025; not re-verified this session]; Hochul backed 2026 measures for a gambling mental-health institute and to keep minors off sports-betting apps; the 18+ age for VLTs vs 21+ for casinos/mobile remains a legislative target. Advertising rules bar targeting under-21s and 'risk-free' language [NYSGC 2024 regulations; not re-verified]. Credit-card funding of mobile accounts remains permitted, with recurring bills to prohibit it [unverified].

**Payments reality.** This is a card/ACH/wallet market (debit, ACH, PayPal/Venmo-type wallets, PayNearMe/cash at casino cages); there is no mobile-money dimension. The 51% tax makes payment-processing cost a material share of operator contribution, which is why promo spend and deposit incentives in NY are thin relative to lower-tax states.

**Read-through for an operator.** New York is the deepest US sports pool ($100bn cumulative mobile handle passed in July 2026; $9.1bn cumulative GGR; $4.65bn to education) but a closed one: no new mobile licence window exists, the 51% rate and $25m fee were set via a 'highest-tax-wins' RFA, and sub-scale books (BetRivers, theScore, Bally Bet: 3.6% of handle combined) are shrinking. Realistic entry routes are B2B supply (platform, trading, content) to the eight incumbents, retail/sportsbook partnerships with the three downstate licensees, or waiting for an iGaming bill — which would most likely allocate skins to existing casino, racino, tribal and mobile licensees rather than new entrants.

segments.name: Mobile sports wagering
segments.headline: Record $2.79bn handle and $258.1m GGR; FanDuel/DraftKings 71% of handle, Fanatics the only share gainer; FYTD GGR down ~3.5% on hold.
narrative: **Volume and revenue.** The NYSGC's statewide monthly report (posted 6 Nov) shows October mobile handle of $2,787,474,078, the highest monthly figure recorded by any US state, up 5.5% on October 2025's prior record of ~$2.64bn and 16.1% on September's $2.40bn. GGR of $258,123,128 rose 8.1% YoY and 61.9% MoM, the third-best month since the January 2022 launch; the MoM jump is almost entirely hold normalisation (9.26% vs 6.6% in September, when six of eight books earned less than a year earlier). Weekly data corroborate the trajectory: $619.4m/$49.2m (w/e 4 Oct, 7.9% hold), $615.1m/$63.3m (w/e 18 Oct) and a fiscal-year-high $656.2m/$79.4m (w/e 25 Oct, 12.1% hold). Including $5.0m of retail handle and $0.6m of retail GGR at upstate casino books, total October sports wagering was $2,792.4m handle and $258.7m GGR.

**Tax.** New York taxes mobile GGR at 51% on a cash basis with no promotional deductions; October's 'net revenue to education' was $131,676,346 (51% × GGR + $33,551 prior-period adjustment), versus $121.8m in October 2025. Implied October tax by operator (est.): FanDuel $58.1m, DraftKings $41.8m, Fanatics $12.2m, BetMGM $8.0m, Caesars $6.7m, the three small books $4.9m combined. Calendar-2026 tax has already passed $1bn for a third consecutive year, but FY2026/27 receipts are $25.1m behind last year's pace at the half-way point because hold has compressed: April–October GGR is $1.37bn on $15.35bn of handle (8.90%) versus $1.41bn on $14.39bn (9.83%) a year earlier. For the state, handle growth of ~7% is not translating into revenue; for operators, the 51% rate means every point of hold lost is borne roughly half by Albany.

**Market shares.** FanDuel remains the only book ever to clear $1bn of monthly handle in New York ($1,022.7m, +1.7% YoY), but its handle share slipped from 38.1% to 36.7%, while an 11.14% hold gave it 44.1% of GGR ($113.9m, +13.3%). DraftKings posted a record $948.7m (+1.1%; 34.0% share) but an 8.63% hold cut GGR 1.2% to $81.9m. Fanatics was the growth story: $321.4m (+56.3%) for an 11.5% share, adding $115.7m of the market's $144.8m YoY handle increase, although a 7.48% hold (9.08% a year ago) limited GGR growth to +28.8% ($24.0m). BetMGM grew 16.4% to $218.2m (GGR $15.6m, 7.1% hold); Caesars was flat at $175.6m (GGR $13.1m, -0.6%); BetRivers $50.5m (-4.8%; GGR $4.5m); Penn's theScore Bet $35.9m (-40.5% against ESPN Bet's prior-year figure; GGR $3.6m, +5.7% on a 10% hold); Bally Bet $14.5m (-12.3%; GGR $1.5m, +27.4%). The combined share of the three sub-scale books is 3.6% of handle, confirming that the 51% rate and the absence of promotional deductions make it nearly impossible for a challenger to buy share profitably — Fanatics being the exception because it is funding share with group-level balance sheet.

**Structure of the licence.** Nine platform licences were awarded through the 2021 competitive RFA (which scored bids on tax rate, producing the 51% outcome); WynnBET and Resorts World Bet have since exited and ESPN Bet was rebranded to theScore Bet, leaving eight live skins. Each licensee paid a $25m fee for a 10-year term running from January 2022 [statute, not re-verified this session]; there is no mechanism for additional licences absent new legislation. Cumulative mobile handle crossed $100bn in July 2026 with $9.12bn of GGR and $4.65bn remitted to education (secondary compilation of NYSGC data).

**Product and content.** New York permits pre-match, in-play and parlay betting on professional and out-of-state college sports; wagering on in-state college teams and on college player props is prohibited, and official-league-data requirements apply to in-play markets [statutory framework, not re-verified]. Same-game parlays are the hold engine — FanDuel's 11%+ hold versus Caesars/BetMGM/Fanatics at ~7% is almost entirely mix. Retail sportsbooks at the four upstate casinos (10% tax) are immaterial at $0.6m GGR.

**Commercial implication.** New York is a volume-not-margin market. Our rough contribution math at a 9% blended hold, 51% tax, ~1.5–2% of handle in payment/processing and platform fees and modest promo leaves a top-two operator with a positive but thin margin and everyone below #3 close to or below break-even. For B2Tech the actionable angles are (i) B2B trading/risk, pricing and SGP content licensed to incumbents, (ii) a retail sportsbook or kiosk partnership with a downstate licensee once Metropolitan Park and Bally's open, and (iii) positioning for any future iGaming skin allocation, which Addabbo's S2614 would have tied to existing licensees.

**Segment outlook.** November and December should produce the two highest handle months of the year (NFL/NBA/college overlap); if hold reverts to the 9–10% range, Q4 FY2026/27 tax should recover the $25m shortfall. Structural growth is now mid-single-digit handle with hold-driven GGR volatility; the main swing factor is the Kalshi litigation — if sports event contracts remain untaxed and unlicensed in New York through 2027, incremental handle leakage from the regulated books is a real, if unquantified, risk.

segments.name: Commercial casinos (downstate & upstate)
segments.headline: RWNYC's first October as a full casino lifts statewide GGR to $194.9m and tax to $78.8m; the property is scaling floor faster than win, and owes the state $80.6m in disputed racing levies.
narrative: **Statewide result.** Five commercial casinos reported $194.9m of GGR in October, up 248% from $56.0m in October 2025 and 5.8% from $184.3m in September. Slots/ETG contributed $135.3m (+214.1% vs $43.1m), live table games $58.3m (+399.6% vs $11.7m), poker $740,441 and retail sports wagering $593,224. Gaming tax for the month was ~$78.8m, an effective 40.4% of GGR — and our bottom-up reconstruction (56%/30% on RWNYC's $89.3m slots and $45.0m tables = $63.5m; 30%/10% on the upstate $46.0m slots, $13.3m tables and $1.3m poker/sports = $15.3m) matches the Commission's figure to the decimal, which confirms both the rate structure and the product split.

**Resorts World New York City (Genting).** The Queens property, previously the state's largest VLT facility, began reporting as a commercial casino in April 2026 after its 15 Dec 2025 licence award and launched live tables that month. October GGR was $134.3m (+6.0% MoM from $126.7m): $89.3m slots/ETG and $45.0m tables on an average of 275 tables (242 in September). Cumulative commercial GGR is $794.3m through October (average $113.5m/month, range $122–136m since the first full month in May) and $859.6m through 15 November, by which point the floor had 4,137 machines and 345 tables. The capacity build is diluting productivity: machines up 61% May–October to 4,024 average daily units while machine revenue fell 9.5% and win per unit per day dropped from $1,275 to $716. Against its bid projection of $2.2bn GGR by 2027, the current run-rate is ~$1.5–1.6bn (est.). Implied October 2025 VLT net win at the property was ~$83m (est., derived from the 37% reported vs 4% like-for-like VLT decline), so conversion plus tables has lifted the site's win by ~60% — meaningful, but short of the step-change the state's $5.5bn-by-2033 downstate forecast requires.

**The racing-support dispute.** Downstate licensees are statutorily required to fund >$150m a year of support payments to NYRA; until Metropolitan Park and Bally's open (~2030), RWNYC carries the entire obligation, cumulatively >$500m. Genting's position is that its 56% slot bid was inclusive of racing support and that the payments are deductible from gaming tax; the state says they are a separate obligation and that paying both would be required by law. The Commission's financial disclosures show RWNYC $80.6m in arrears through October, growing ~$13m a month and projected to exceed $180m by June 2027; RWNYC says stacking the levy would take its effective slot tax to ~72%. Spring 2026 legislation let the NYSGC pay NYRA out of RWNYC's tax receipts; an October 2026 interim agreement now has RWNYC paying NYRA directly while remitting only part of its tax, with the Governor's office explicitly reserving the deficiency claim. The MTA, which shares downstate casino tax with education, stands to lose up to ~$150m. Genting has signalled it could abandon the $3.3bn phase-two expansion if forced to pay both. The interim deal expires at the end of the June 2027 session, making this a 2027 budget/legislative item.

**Upstate casinos.** The four upstate properties won $60.6m, +8.2% YoY: Rivers Schenectady $20.2m (+14.2%), Resorts World Catskills $15.7m (+10.6%), del Lago $15.0m (+3.9%) and Tioga Downs $9.7m (+0.5%). All four pay 30% on slots/ETG (reduced from the original 37–45% regional rates via petitions permitted under the 2021 law) and 10% on tables and sports; tax is allocated 80% to education/property-tax relief, 10% to host municipality/county and 10% to regional counties. A 2025 study cited in the Hudson Valley context projected that three downstate casinos could cut upstate casino revenue by up to 76% — October's upstate growth suggests no cannibalisation yet, because RWNYC's catchment is NYC proper, but Resorts World Catskills is the most exposed once Metropolitan Park opens.

**Pipeline.** Metropolitan Park (Hard Rock/Cohen; $8.1bn; ~50 acres of Citi Field parking) and Bally's Bronx ($4bn; Ferry Point) hold licences at 25%/10% and 30%/10% respectively, each having paid the $500m minimum fee, with 2030 openings targeted. Metropolitan Park's design review at NYC's Public Design Commission was deferred on 23 Nov for the second time after five hours of testimony; a vote is set for 30 Nov, and the PDC cannot revoke the state licence. A Queens residents' suit against the licence award (20 Mar 2026) is pending. RWNYC's supplemental application asks that its 56%/30% rates be equalised downward once lower-taxed competitors open — a request the state has not granted and which, combined with the racing dispute, makes downstate tax policy the single most consequential open item in NY land-based gaming.

**Commercial implication.** The downstate market is a licensed three-player oligopoly for 15–25 years with no further licences available; entry is via supply (systems, EGMs, ETGs, cashless/payments, loyalty) or by partnering with licensees on sportsbook/retail. segments.headline: VLT net win $132.1m (-37% reported, +4% like-for-like) as RWNYC leaves the lottery system; Empire City now the largest racino at $52.3m.
narrative: **Statewide VLT.** Video gaming machines at the eight remaining video lottery facilities generated $132.1m of net win in October, 37% below October 2025 because RWNYC's ~$83m (est.) of VLT win migrated to the commercial casino ledger in April; on a like-for-like basis the sector grew ~4% with 11,373 machines in operation, and was up 5.8% on September's $124.8m. VLT facilities operate under the Lottery framework (Tax Law §1612): the Commission's central system runs the games, net win is split by statute between education, the operator's agent commission, a marketing allowance and racing support, and the minimum age is 18 (versus 21 for casinos and mobile) — a gap legislators have proposed to close.

**Empire City (MGM, Yonkers).** Now the state's largest racino: October credits played $749.2m (incl. $4.86m free play), net win $52,258,251 (+2.5% YoY vs $51.0m; +7.6% MoM vs $48.6m) on an average 4,516 machines at $373 win/unit/day (Oct-25: 4,487 at $367). Distribution: $26.39m to education, $20.64m agent commission, $5.23m marketing allowance. Full fiscal-year sales and prize payout are n/a in this review.

**Racing and ADW.** Pari-mutuel racing (NYRA at Aqueduct/Belmont/Saratoga; harness tracks) is regulated by the NYSGC and increasingly dependent on statutory transfers: VLT racing-support percentages and the >$150m/year downstate casino racing-support obligation at the centre of the RWNYC dispute. **Commercial implication.** The VLT channel is a closed, state-run system (central determinant games, no third-party operators) — supply opportunities are limited to game content and systems vendors already on the Lottery's approved list. segments.name: Licensing & tax regime
segments.headline: Closed licence stacks in every vertical; the highest headline sports-betting tax in the US (51%), bespoke bid-based casino rates (25–56% slots), and statutory revenue splits that make Albany the senior partner in every operator's P&L.
narrative: **Constitutional and statutory base.** Gambling is prohibited by the state constitution except as expressly authorised: the Lottery (1966), pari-mutuel racing, charitable gaming, and — via the 2013 amendment — up to seven commercial casinos 'as prescribed by the legislature'. The Upstate NY Gaming Economic Development Act (2013) created the four upstate licences; the FY2023 budget (April 2022) released the remaining three for the downstate region; mobile sports wagering was authorised in the FY2022 budget (April 2021) as an extension of casino sports wagering with servers located at licensed casinos. Online casino gaming has no authorisation; online lottery (draw games via the Lottery app) and ADW are permitted.

**Mobile sports wagering.** Platform licences were awarded in November 2021 via a competitive RFA that scored tax rate heavily, producing a 51% GGR rate (cash basis, no promo deduction, no carry-forward of negative months within the statutory formula other than prior-period adjustments) and a $25m licence fee per platform for a 10-year term [fee/term not re-verified this session]. Nine licences were issued; eight remain active. The Commission publishes weekly and monthly handle, GGR and 'net revenue to education' by operator — a disclosure regime that is unusually transparent by US standards. Retail sportsbooks at the four upstate casinos pay 10% of GGR. There is no provision for additional mobile licences, and the 51% rate has survived every budget cycle since 2022 despite operator lobbying for promotional deductions.

**Commercial casinos.** Upstate: statutory slot rates of 37–45% by region were made reducible to 30% by petition in the 2021 amendment; all four now pay 30% slots/ETG and 10% tables/poker/sports, allocated 80/10/10 to education-property tax relief, host locality and regional counties. Downstate: the law set a $500m minimum licence fee and minimum rates of 25% slots / 10% tables, with bidders free to offer more; the December 2025 awards locked in RWNYC at 56%/30%, Bally's at 30%/10% and Metropolitan Park at 25%/10% for the licence term (15–25 years per trade reporting; [term not re-verified]). Downstate tax is split between education and the MTA. The racing-support payment obligation (>$150m/year across the three licensees, borne solely by RWNYC until ~2030) sits on top of these rates and is the subject of the current dispute. RWNYC has asked the state to harmonise rates downward once lower-rate competitors open; nothing has been granted.

**Video lottery.** Facility licences are issued to racetracks and OTB corporations; net win is distributed by a statutory tiered schedule per facility (Empire City: education 54–60%, agent commission 26–32%, 10% marketing allowance, 4% racing support/purses), with host-municipality aid ($19.6m/year to Yonkers) and a minimum age of 18. There is no bid-based tax; the operator is effectively a commissioned agent of the Lottery.

**Tribal gaming.** Seneca (western NY), Oneida (Turning Stone region) and St Regis Mohawk nations operate Class III casinos under federal compacts with exclusivity zones and revenue-share payments to the state; GGR is not disclosed (n/a). Any iGaming bill will have to navigate tribal exclusivity provisions.

**Sweepstakes and unlicensed online.** New York enacted a prohibition on online sweepstakes casinos (RPWBL §912) [enacted late 2025; not re-verified this session], joining a cohort of states closing the dual-currency loophole; licensed operators and the Lottery's own promotions are carved out. Combined with the prediction-market litigation, the enforcement posture is clearly toward channelling all real-money play into NYSGC-licensed products — but with no iGaming product to channel it into.

**Commercial implication.** The regime rewards incumbency and balance sheet. Entry fees are high ($25m mobile, $500m downstate casino) and tax rates are set by auction rather than by policy, so late entrants inherit rates optimised by the winners. B2Tech should model New York as a supply and partnership market, and treat the 2027 session (racing-support fix, possible downstate rate harmonisation, iGaming reboot, prediction-market bill) as the next window in which the rules can actually move.

segments.name: Regulatory direction: iGaming, prediction markets, responsible gambling & payments
segments.headline: Expansion is stalled (no iGaming before 2027), enforcement is escalating (Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase/Gemini, sweepstakes), and the fiscal fight over downstate levies will dominate the 2027 session.
narrative: **iGaming.** Sen. Joseph Addabbo's S2614 — online slots, blackjack, roulette, baccarat, live dealer (with studios required in-state), NYSGC licensing, skins for commercial casinos, racinos, tribes and mobile operators, projected by the sponsor at ~$475m/year of tax — did not get a committee hearing or floor vote before the session ended on 4 June 2026. Addabbo shelved it after Gov. Hochul declined to engage ('will review any legislation that passes'); he intends to reintroduce in 2027. The Governor instead backed a gambling mental-health institute and measures to keep minors off sports-betting apps. Realistically, iGaming requires executive sponsorship in an Executive Budget; absent that, New York stays the largest US state without online casino through at least FY2027/28.

**Prediction markets.** Sequence: NYSGC cease-and-desist to Kalshi (24 Oct 2025) → Kalshi sues the Commission in SDNY; emergency injunction denied → AG Letitia James sues Coinbase (which offers Kalshi markets) and Gemini (21 Apr 2026) → Addabbo's S9414, banning sports and election contracts, advances 6–0 in committee (20 May 2026) but stalls → Governor and AG sue Kalshi in state court (31 Jul 2026) seeking injunction, disgorgement, restitution and treble fines (press estimates ≥$36bn including $100,000 per unlawful wager); Kalshi removes to federal court → a July 2026 federal ruling holds the state can reach sports contracts; AG also moves against Polymarket → AG refiles TRO motion seeking to bar Kalshi from offering sports, culture, election and other contracts 'within or from New York' and to under-21s → 23 Nov 2026: Justice Melissa Crane denies the TRO; the case proceeds to a January 2027 hearing. Both Kalshi and Polymarket are headquartered in New York, so a 'from New York' injunction would have national reach. For licensed sportsbooks the stakes are straightforward: untaxed, 18+ sports event contracts compete directly with a product taxed at 51% and restricted to 21+.

**Responsible gambling and advertising.** NYSGC's sports wagering advertising regulations prohibit targeting under-21s (including on college campuses), bar 'risk-free'/'free' bet language, and require problem-gambling messaging and the HOPEline number in all advertising [2024 rules; not re-verified this session]. Operators fund problem-gambling services through the tax allocation and must offer deposit, wager and time limits plus statewide self-exclusion. The 2026 session produced the mental-health-institute initiative; age harmonisation (raising VLT play from 18 to 21) and affordability-style measures remain live proposals. Compared with the UK or Spain, New York's RG regime is light on affordability checks and heavy on advertising-content rules and age-gating.

**Payments.** Funding methods are debit cards, ACH/online banking, PayPal/Venmo-type wallets, prepaid Play+ cards and cash at casino cages (PayNearMe); credit cards are not statutorily barred for mobile wagering, and bills to prohibit credit-card funding have been introduced but not enacted [unverified]. There is no mobile-money layer; the commercial issue is that at a 51% tax, processing costs of 1.5–3% of deposits are a material share of operator margin, which is why NY books push ACH and wallets. Cashless gaming on casino floors is permitted under NYSGC rules and is being deployed at RWNYC [unverified detail].

**Fiscal politics.** Three items converge in the 2027 session (January–June): (i) the RWNYC racing-support settlement, where the interim agreement expires and the arrears will be ~$180m; (ii) RWNYC's request to harmonise downstate tax rates downward, which would cut state receipts from the only operating downstate casino; and (iii) the Executive Budget's treatment of gaming revenue after FYTD mobile tax has slipped $25m behind plan. Our reading is that Albany will protect education/MTA receipts first — the probability of a lower tax rate for RWNYC is low, while the probability of a legislated fix that lets the Commission pay NYRA from the commercial gaming revenue fund (as RWNYC proposed in June 2026) is moderate.

**Enforcement posture.** The Commission's tools are cease-and-desist letters, licence conditions and referral to the AG; the AG has become the primary enforcer against unlicensed online activity (prediction markets, crypto exchanges, offshore). For a licensed operator this is a favourable environment — the state is actively defending the regulated perimeter — but the pace of court action (14 months from C&D to a January 2027 hearing) means leakage persists for at least one more NFL season.

RWNYC's live tables are working: $45.0m of table GGR in October (23% of its total) from a standing start in April, with 345 tables by mid-November — evidence that NYC's table demand was unmet under the VLT-only regime.

Fanatics proves share can still move: +56% YoY handle to an 11.5% share, capturing ~80% of market growth, shows that distribution (retail/merch base) can dent the duopoly even at a 51% tax — relevant to any entrant with an existing NY customer base.

The state is actively defending the licensed perimeter: sweepstakes banned, AG litigation against Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase and Gemini, and a Commission cease-and-desist regime — a tailwind for licensed operators if the January 2027 hearing goes the state's way.

Upstate casinos grew 8.2% YoY with no cannibalisation yet from RWNYC, and Empire City VLT win rose 2.5% despite a full casino 15 miles away — the downstate conversion appears, so far, to be expanding the market rather than redistributing it.

Unusually transparent data: weekly operator-level handle, GGR and tax disclosure allows precise market-share and hold benchmarking that most jurisdictions (and all African markets in our coverage) do not offer.

lowlights.text: The 51% mobile tax with no promotional deduction leaves no profitable path for a challenger: the three sub-scale books hold 3.6% of handle and are shrinking (theScore -40.5%, Bally Bet -12.3%, BetRivers -4.8%); two of nine original licensees have already exited.

Hold compression is eroding the state's take: FYTD GGR -3.5% on +6.7% handle (hold 8.90% vs 9.83%), tax $25.1m behind plan — a revenue-hungry Albany is more likely to tighten (e.g., prediction-market bans, VLT age rise) than to cut rates or allow promo deductions.

RWNYC's $80.6m racing-support arrears (rising ~$13m/month, >$180m by June 2027) and its 72%-effective-rate argument show the downstate tax stack is unresolved; the outcome will set the economics for all three downstate licensees and the MTA/education revenue they fund.

Downstate ramp is below bid: RWNYC's ~$1.5–1.6bn run-rate (est.) vs a $2.2bn 2027 projection, with win/unit/day down 44% (to $716) as the floor expanded 61% — a warning for the state's $5.5bn-by-2033 downstate forecast and for suppliers sizing orders on bid numbers.

No iGaming before 2027 at the earliest and no executive sponsorship; the largest US state market by sports handle has zero regulated online casino GGR, and any eventual bill is likely to allocate skins to incumbents.

Prediction markets remain live and untaxed in New York after the 23 Nov TRO denial; with Kalshi and Polymarket both headquartered in the state, the January 2027 hearing is binary for both leakage risk and the precedent for other states.

Two of the three downstate resorts face local friction: Metropolitan Park's design vote has been deferred twice and a residents' lawsuit is pending, pushing 2030 opening risk to the right and extending RWNYC's solo liability for racing support.

forecast.intro: The October print moves our FY2026/27 view in two directions: mobile handle growth is running ahead of our prior mid-single-digit assumption (+6.7% FYTD) but GGR is below it because hold has fallen ~90bp, so the state's mobile tax line will finish close to flat on FY2025/26 (~$1.1bn) rather than up. On land-based, RWNYC's conversion lifts statewide commercial casino GGR to a ~$2.2–2.3bn annualised run-rate (est.) from ~$0.7bn in FY2025/26, with upstate flat-to-up mid-single digits and VLT net win settling at ~$1.5–1.6bn annualised (est.) ex-RWNYC. The moving parts are hold normalisation in Q4, RWNYC's table ramp versus slot dilution, and — most importantly — the legislative resolution of the racing-support levy, which determines whether downstate gaming tax lands near 47% or 56%+ of RWNYC's slot win.

forecast.view: **Market.** We expect calendar-2026 mobile handle of ~$26–27bn (est.) and GGR of ~$2.3–2.4bn (est.), with Q4 hold reverting toward 9–10% on NFL/NBA parlay mix; structural handle growth slows to 3–6% a year from 2027 as the market matures and prediction-market substitution bites at the margin. FanDuel/DraftKings' combined handle share drifts toward ~68% as Fanatics approaches 13–15%; expect at least one more exit among the three smallest books before licence renewal. **Land-based.** RWNYC should stabilise at $1.5–1.7bn GGR in 2027 (est.) — below its $2.2bn bid — with the slot floor consolidating and tables carrying growth; the upstate four grow low-single digits until Metropolitan Park opens (~2030), after which Resorts World Catskills and Empire City face material cannibalisation. **Rules.** Base case for the 2027 session: (1) a legislated racing-support fix that routes NYRA payments through the commercial gaming revenue fund with partial credit to RWNYC — **no cut to the 56%/30% headline rates**; (2) no iGaming unless the Executive Budget sponsors it (we put the probability at ~25%), and if it comes, skins tied to existing casino/racino/mobile/tribal licensees at a 30%+ tax; (3) a statutory ban on sports event contracts (S9414-type) if the January court outcome is unfavourable to the state, otherwise the AG litigation continues through 2027; (4) VLT age raised to 21 and credit-card funding restrictions as RG add-ons. **Leverage/fiscal direction.** The state's gaming tax base rises in FY2026/27 only because of RWNYC; with mobile tax flat and the MTA short up to ~$150m from the racing dispute, the fiscal bias is toward **extracting more from existing licensees, not toward liberalising entry or rates.** For B2Tech the implication is to prioritise B2B supply and downstate partnerships over any direct-licence ambition in New York over the next 24 months.
